content.text:
I checked 13 claims against the record and flagged none.

- **How shoppers fared:** "Shoppers saw nothing wrong" is the closest call. The logs only reach 03:26, and they show the usual ClientDisconnected errors, with the error rate typically 1.00% after the stop against 0.50% before. I counted it as supported because the record expects that statement, tells the writer to cite those log lines for it, and records no customer loss.
- **Root cause:** The claim that the scrape configuration still looked for "metrics" is stated without a hedge in causal_chain 3. It still holds together:
  - S1 says the scrape selects the target by the port's name.
  - D1 shows the deploy changed only the values file, so the scrape configuration was as before.
  - Metrics were collected up to 03:20 under the old name, and came back after the rollback.

  The root_cause field itself says it rests on F1 and is unverified.

I didn't judge the action items or the "had it been otherwise" sentences, since they propose things or describe what-ifs.

supported.quote: The scrape configuration finds the shop's metrics target by the port's name, not its number, and the deploy renamed that port in deploy/values-production.yaml from metrics to http-metrics without changing the name deploy/scrape.yaml selects, which is still metrics. The selector then matched no port, and the scraper had nothing left to collect. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, and the monitoring setup most likely still looked for the old name, so it stopped collecting them.

Any deploy that names the metrics port differently from the name the scrape configuration looks for, whether the same rename going out again or one of the two files changing without the other, would quietly stop the shop's metrics being collected again without raising any error.
Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped being collected
No sign was seen that anyone using the shop had a problem. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and no samples covered the minutes after they stopped.

The deploy of revision 9f4ad14 at {P2.1} changed one value in deploy/values-production.yaml: it renamed the metrics port from metrics to http-metrics and left the port number at {D1.1}. When read at {T13.1}, all {T13.2} replicas were running that revision.
The earlier deploy of revision e283ba3 at {P1.1}. Metrics were collected with it in place up to the minute at {T5.2}. Once the rollback put that revision back, the metrics could be read again.
The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics target by the port's name and was still looking for metrics, so after the rename it matched no port and had nothing to collect.

No check was seen that would catch the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml no longer matching the name the scrape configuration selects. The values file's own comment says nothing in the shop reads that name, and that a name nothing matches fails silently. A rename in one file could therefore ship without the other file changing.

The MetricsAbsent alert fired {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval, the scraping allowance and the minute-level dating of the stop can explain. The record does not show what took the extra time.
